circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke and home to the Formula One season finale since 2009. It represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: A street circuit encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, this venue hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various support categories including the Supercars Championship round. The track holds FIA Grade 1 certification, meeting the highest international standards for motorsport facilities.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Styria, the 4. 326 km Austrian circuit was originally established as the Österreichring, hosting the country's grand prix annually from 1970 to 1987. Following extensive modifications and a name change to the A1-Ring, the venue returned to the Formula One calendar from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street-based racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital, situated alongside Baku Boulevard, with each lap measuring 6. 003 km to rank as the fourth-longest Formula One track. The circuit debuted in motorsport with the 2016 European Grand Prix before being designated as the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: The Bahrain International Circuit, established in 2004, is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. Beyond its primary F1 role, the facility accommodates various motorsports including drag racing, GP2 competition, and endurance events, while briefly featuring Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 to 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Barcelona-Catalunya circuit in Montmeló spans 4. 657 kilometres and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for teams. The venue accommodates 140,700 spectators and holds the highest FIA safety classification for racing facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated in Belgium's Wallonia region near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a fixture of Formula One since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The venue currently hosts the Belgian Grand Prix annually, with its only recent absences occurring in 2003 and 2006, following a continuous run of races from 1985 onward.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361 km circuit serves as the permanent home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sportscar championships and North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue primarily recognized for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has expanded its calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix, an electric racing championship that began in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, located in England near Northamptonshire, has been the traditional venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After sharing the British Grand Prix with Aintree and Brands Hatch between 1955 and 1986, Silverstone became its permanent home from 1987 onward and continues to stage major international motorsport events including MotoGP races.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted the pioneering Formula One Hungarian Grand Prix in 1986, marking the championship's first race in Eastern Europe. Built in just eight months starting from late 1985, faster than any other Formula One venue at the time, the circuit was constructed outside the city near a highway after government authorities rejected plans for a street course in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949 (except 1980 during renovations) and remains one of Formula One's oldest continuously featured circuits, earning its reputation as "the Temple of Speed" for its notably lengthy straights and fast-cornering layout.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport facility operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, hosting major international racing events with a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track is particularly renowned for staging Formula One and Super Formula championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course situated in Paradise, Nevada, that navigates through the iconic boulevard lined with the city's premier hospitality venues and entertainment destinations. The layout incorporates several recognizable landmarks including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it winds through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez commemorates two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate accidents. The circuit resumed hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, now on a revised layout compared to its previous configurations that last saw the race in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary track constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring 3. 363 miles of racing surface with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed specifically by Apex Circuit Design for Formula One, the venue joined the F1 calendar in 2022 and has since become the primary home of the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street layout winding through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the harborfront roads of the Principality of Monaco. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is predominantly known as the Monte Carlo circuit since most of the track traverses the Monte Carlo area.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining the Formula One calendar in 2021, though the partnership concluded in 2026. The track, situated near the North Sea, has undergone several name changes throughout its history.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Located north of Doha in Qatar, the Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419 km track featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km circuit that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features a karting facility dedicated to another celebrated Brazilian racing driver.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline that has been the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021. The circuit also began hosting an international electric racing championship event in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang neighborhoods into its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is a 4. 657 km track located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, featuring a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test various driving skills. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track regularly hosts major motorsport events including MotoGP's Americas round, the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, and NASCAR competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai-British driver Alexander Albon currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 Grand Prix victories across 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24-hour victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli has competed in Formula One since 2025 as a member of the Mercedes team, during which time he has secured eight Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, where he competes at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One with Audi, competing at the highest level of motorsport after progressing through various junior categories.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing experience from a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his time with Mercedes, and has secured ten Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races in Formula One with the Alpine team. He represents his nation in one of motorsport's premier racing series.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan races in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category with Nielsen Racing while holding a reserve role at Haas in Formula One, having appeared in seven championship rounds during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French driver currently racing for Alpine, previously secured a Grand Prix victory at Monza in 2020 while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar represents France in Formula One while driving for Red Bull Racing, bringing both French and Algerian heritage to the sport.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British driver competing for Ferrari who has equalled Michael Schumacher's record of seven world championship titles. He holds multiple Formula One records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved significant success in endurance motorsport by winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport talent, currently drives for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc represents Monaco in Formula One racing for Ferrari, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. The driver finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen, a Danish driver known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate periods from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship as a factory driver for BMW with WRT, while also undertaking part-time NASCAR Cup Series duties with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has secured 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon currently races for Haas in Formula One after previously competing for Alpine, where he achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One. He finished second in the 2023 championship while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his extensive 15-season career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian driver competing in Formula One for McLaren, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo is an Australian driver who spent 14 seasons competing in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" throughout his career. He secured eight Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British Formula One competitor, drives for Mercedes and has claimed seven Grand Prix victories during his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. Following a two-year Formula One stint from 2023 to 2024, he has transitioned to sports car racing, having previously driven LMP2 machinery for Era Motorsports in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently racing in Formula One with Aston Martin, competing at the sport's highest level.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda transitioned from a full-time Formula One career spanning 2021 to 2025 into a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls starting in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole representative in Formula One history, raced in the championship between 2022 and 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He currently holds the position of reserve driver for the American-based team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based squad operated as Renault's official works team from 2021 onwards under the Alpine marque, representing the French manufacturer's performance-focused automotive brand. Following Renault's withdrawal from the sport after 2025, the team transitioned from factory-backed status to an independent competitor, continuing to race from its traditional English headquarters.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, with the current operation run by AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, is the longest-running and most dominant outfit in Formula One history, participating in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. The team's iconic emblem, featuring a rearing horse, has become synonymous with the pinnacle of motorsport excellence and Italian racing tradition.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas established this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the squad making its competitive debut during the 2016 season. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner, who held the position from the team's founding through January 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Swiss motorsport engineering outfit Sauber, established in 1970, competed in Formula One from 1993 as an independent constructor before transitioning to Audi's new F1 project. The team achieved notable endurance racing success, including overall victory at Le Mans in 1989, but departed the sport in 2025 having competed for three decades as one of motorsport's longest-serving constructors.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking, operating as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Bahraini ownership through Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes-AMG Petronas, operating under a German licence from Brackley, represents the automotive giant's long-standing involvement in Formula One since 1954 as both constructor and engine supplier. The team transitioned to a tri-ownership structure in 2022, with equal stakes held by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. Known historically as the "Silver Arrows," Mercedes-badged squads have maintained a prominent presence throughout the sport's modern era.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as Red Bull GmbH's second works team. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, it operates alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-team structure in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the squad represents the Austrian conglomerate's second racing operation in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England but licensed under Austria, has competed in Formula One since 2005 as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner led the squad from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies taking over as team principal in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, set to compete as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, is a British constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's prior racing venture. Headquartered on a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has maintained its operations from this location since its inception.
